results.question: An adult is choking on food right now. They are awake but cannot speak, breathe or cough. They are not pregnant and I can reach around their waist. Another person is beside me. What do we do?
results.reference:
Guide: Adult choking
Scope: Adults only. Children and infants need age-appropriate instructions. Follow the emergency dispatcher.
Act immediately when a choking adult cannot cough, speak or breathe effectively.
Get help: Weak or absent coughing, inability to speak, blue or pale skin, or unresponsiveness require emergency help.
1. If they can cough effectively, encourage coughing and stay with them.
2. For an ineffective cough or inability to speak or breathe, have someone call the local emergency number now.
3. Support their chest, lean them forward and give up to 5 separate blows between the shoulder blades with your hand heel.
4. If still choking, stand behind them. Put a fist just above the navel, grasp it, and give up to 5 inward-and-upward abdominal thrusts. Use chest thrusts instead during pregnancy or if you cannot reach around them.
5. Alternate these sets until the blockage clears or they become unresponsive. If unresponsive, lower them onto a firm, flat surface and start CPR, beginning with compressions, following dispatcher instructions. Never sweep the mouth blindly.
Sources: American Red Cross: Choking (https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/adult-child-choking)

2. Si la tos no es eficaz o no puede hablar o respirar, pida a alguien que llame ahora al número local de emergencias.
3. Sostenga su pecho, inclínelo hacia delante y dé hasta 5 golpes separados entre los omóplatos con la base de la palma de la mano.
